senses.gloss: प्लु [cf. Gk. πλέω, πλεϝω, πλύνω; Old Lat. per-plovere; Lat. pluit, pluvius; Lith. plauti; Angl.Sax. flovan; Germ., flawjan, flawên, vlouwen &c.]
प्लुत mfn. floated, floating or swimming in (loc.), bathed, overflowed, submerged, covered or filled with (instr. or comp.), Yājñ.; MBh.; R. &c.
protracted, prolated or lengthened (as a vowel) to 3 Mātrās (q.v.), Prāt.; Pāṇ. i, 2, 27 esp.; ŚrS. &c. (also said of a kind of measure, Cat.)
flown, R.
leaped, leaping, MBh.; Hariv.
प्लुत n. a flood, deluge (pl.), Hariv.
leaping, moving by leaps, MBh.; R.; Vcar.
capering (one of a horse's paces), L.
प्लुत—गति f. moving by leaps, Dhātup.
प्लुत—गति m. a hare, L.
प्लुत—त्व n. See उदग्र-प्लुत-त्व.
प्लुत—मेरु m. (in music) a kind of measure, Saṃgīt.
प्लुत—वत् mfn. one who has leaped or jumped, R.; Hariv.
प्लुति f. overflowing, a flood, Var.
prolation (of a vowel, cf. प्लुत), Prāt.; Pāṇ., Sch.; ŚrS.
a leap, jump, Śak. i, 7 v.l. (also met.; cf. मण्डूक-प्ल्˚)
capering, curvet (one of a horse's paces), L.
प्लुगि and प्लोक् ind. onomat. sounds used for a Nidhana, Drāhy.

प्लुस् cl. 4. P. प्लुस्यति, to burn, Dhātup. xxvi, 107 (v.l. for प्लुष्);
to share, Vop.
प्लुक्षि m. fire, Uṇ. iii, 155, Sch.
the burning of a house (?), L.
oil, L.
प्लु॑षि m. a species of noxious insect, RV.; VS.; ŚBr. (a flying white-ant, L.)
प्लुष्ट mfn. burned, scorched, singed, Ṛtus.; Var.; Suśr.
frozen, Vcar.
प्लुष्टाय Nom. Ā. ˚यते, Pat. on Pāṇ. iii, 1, 17.
